questions.question: Which of the following instruments is used for the visual examination of eardrum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. __Otoscope__.**

 
• An** Otoscope** is an instrument with lighting and magnifying systems used for visual examination of the tympanic membrane and the canal connecting it to the exterior of the body.
 
• **Otolaryngology**, also called otorhinolaryngology, medical speciality concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the ear, nose, and throat.
 
• A **phonograph**, also called record player, an instrument for reproducing sounds by means of the vibration of a stylus, or needle, following a groove on a rotating disc.
 
• The **lie detector**, also called **polygraph**, an instrument for recording physiological phenomena such as blood pressure, pulse rate, and respiration of a human subject as he answers questions put to him by an operator.
 
• **Optometer** is an instrument for measuring the refractive error of an eye.

questions.question: The Barabar Caves, the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, mostly belong to which of the following periods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. the __Maurya Empire__.**

 
• The Barabar Caves are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, mostly dating from the Maurya Empire (322–185 BCE), some with Ashokan inscriptions, located in the **Bela Ganj Block of Gaya district, Bihar**, India, 24 km north of Gaya.
 
• These caves are situated in the twin hills of **Barabar and Nagarjuni.**
 
• Caves of Nagarjuni Hill sometimes are singled out as Nagarjuni Caves. These rock-cut chambers date back to the 3rd century BC, Maurya period, of Ashoka (273-232 BCE) and his son **Dasaratha Maurya.**
 
• The caves were used by ascetics from the Ajivika sect, founded by **Makkali Gosala**, a contemporary of Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism, and of Mahavira, the last and 24th Tirthankara of Jainism.

questions.question: Which of the following countries was declared as a malaria-free country in May 2019 by World Health Organization?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. __Argentina__.**

 
• On 22 May 2019, the World Health Organization (WHO) officially recognized Algeria and Argentina as malaria-free.
 
• **Algeria** is the second country in the WHO African Region and **Argentina **the second country in the WHO Region of the Americas to achieve WHO certification of malaria-free status.
 
• A total of **38 countries** and territories worldwide have now achieved malaria-free status.
 
• **Maldives & Sri Lanka** are the only country in South-East Asia to have received this Malaria-free certification from WHO.

questions.question: Who among the following has the power to promulgate ordinances under Article 123 of the Constitution of India?

options.text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. __The President.__**

__
 
• **Article 123** of the Constitution grants **the President**__ certain lawmaking powers to promulgate Ordinances when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session and hence it is not possible to enact laws in the Parliament.
 
• I**__n the State, the Governor can promulgate an ordinance. Article 213 provides the Governor with this power.__**
 
• The President can only promulgate an Ordinance when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session.
 
• The President cannot promulgate an Ordinance unless he is satisfied that there are circumstances that require taking ‘immediate action'.
 
• Ordinances must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of reassembling or they shall cease to operate.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest bone in the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. __Femur__**.

__
 
• **The femur__**, also called the **thighbone**, the upper bone of the leg or hind leg is the largest bone in the human body.
 
• The head forms a ball-and-socket joint with the hip, being held in place by a ligament within the socket and by strong surrounding ligaments.
 
• A ligament is a tough fibrous band of **connective tissue** that serves to support the internal organs and **hold bones together **in proper articulation at the joints.
 
• Human femurs have been shown to be capable of resisting compression forces of around **800–1,100 kg.**

questions.question: Bugyals are high altitude meadows and pastures in the Himalayan slopes. In which state would you find them most?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. __Uttarakhand__.**

• These meadows are usually seated at high altitudes ranging between 3300 m to 4000 m.

questions.question: According to Global Peace Index 2019, which one of the following is the most peaceful country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. __Iceland.__**

 
• **Iceland **remains the **most peaceful **country in the world, a position it has held since 2008.
 
• It is joined at the top of the index by New Zealand, Austria, Portugal, and Denmark.
 
• **India is ranked 141**. It has slipped 5 places in the past year.
 
• **Bhutan** has recorded the** largest improvement** of any country in the top 20, rising 43 places in the last 12 years.

 **Afghanistan **is now the **least peaceful **country in the world, replacing Syria, which is now the second least peaceful.
 
• South Sudan, Yemen, and Iraq comprise the remaining five least peaceful countries
 
• The **13th edition of the Global Peace Index** ranked 163 independent countries based on their level of peacefulness.
 
• It is produced by the** Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP).**
 
• It measures the state of peace using** three thematic domains** - The level of Societal Safety and Security, the extent of Ongoing Domestic and International Conflict, and the degree of Militarisation.

questions.question: Sanjhi Art is associated to which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. __Uttar Pradesh.__**

questions.question: With how many states/Union Territories does Uttar Pradesh share its borders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3) i.e. 9__.__**

 
• Uttar Pradesh is the only state that shares its boundaries with maximum states.
 
• Uttar Pradesh shares its borders with as many as 9 states/Union Territories,
 
• It also shares an international border with Nepal.
 
• Assam is the only Indian State which shares the border with 7 states. Assam bordering states – West Bengal in the west, Arunachal Pradesh in the northeast, Nagaland, and Manipur in east, Mizoram, Tripura and Meghalaya in the south.
 
• Uttar Pradesh is the Indian State which shares its border with 8 states and 1 union territory which is maximum. Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand in North, Bihar Jharkhand in the east, Rajasthan in West and Madhya Pradesh and Chattisgarh in the south. 
 
• West Bengal In the north it is bounded by the state of Sikkim and the country of Bhutan. To the North-East, it is bounded by the state of Assam. To the East, it is bounded by the country of Bangladesh. To the south, it is bounded by the Bay of Bengal. To the South-West, it is bounded by the state of Odisha. To the West, it is bounded by the states of Jharkhand and Bihar and the North-West, it is bounded by the country Nepal.
 
• Manipur shares it border with 3 states Nagaland, Mizoram, and Assam.
 
• Uttrakhand shares its borders with Tibet in the north, Uttar Pradesh in the south, Nepal in the east, Haryana in the west, and Himachal Pradesh in the North West.
